newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks mixed, trade seen directionless.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks mixed, trade seen directionless.

text.p: Croatian food processor Podravka was a rare attraction in a mixed market on Thursday as volume and turnover dwindled, with traders expecting trade to remain directionless for a while.
"Summer is here and there is nothing to pull the market up. I cannot see any reversal for a week or two," said one trader at a large bank.
Podravka sold 2,027 shares to close 2.04 percent higher at 250 kuna. It traded at 245-288 kuna during the session and one dealer said it could yet go higher.
The company signed a deal on Wednesday night for a 60 million German mark loan at 2.50 percent over Libor, which will be used for repaying old debts at higher rates.
"It was the first serious volume for Podravka in days, so the market evidently reacted to this news. But what could really send it up are positive first half results," the trader said.

Although the company has not yet revealed the size of its 1996 consolidated loss, he said the market had already built it into Podravka's share price. It fell in late May as a result of rumours to well below the 300-kuna issued stock price.
Out of 13 issues, four others also rose, six fell and two ended flat. Volume was more than halved at 4,562 units with turnover fetching no more than 2.4 million kuna.

Zagrebacka Banka's C-series bearer stock led the day's gainers, adding 30 kuna or 3.52 percent to 880 kuna on volume of 65 shares. This series, which is limited, is much in demand because of the guaranteed dividend of 10.5 percent on its 142.86 German mark face value.
"It is surprising that the price is rising just after the dividend payment," said one market watcher. "But it indicates a stronger interest for Zagrebacka in general."

The bank's ordinaries headed down five kuna to 2,015 on volume of 504 units, after gaining 57 kuna on Wednesday. But the preferred E-series lost 10 kuna to 1,500 after a recent rise caused by stronger demand.
Another blue chip Pliva pharmaceuticals, losing one kuna to 484 with 100 units sold and continued to slide in what traders described as a correction after its recent climb.

Both stocks seemed to react to slightly lower prices fetched by their respective global depositary receipts (GDRs) in London. Zagrebacka's GDRs, issued at 10 to each share, fell to $32.375 from $32.625 at close on Wednesday, and Pliva's to $15.95 from $16.01 per 1/5 GDR.

Chocolate maker Kras lost four kuna to 415 with only 300 shares sold as investors seemingly lost interest in it. Kras shares have fallen steadily despite plans, announced earlier this week, to raise 60 million marks from foreign banks for the company's restructuring and development.
The biggest decliner, shipper Jadroplov, fell 12 kuna or 7.5 percent to 148 kuna on volume of 226 shares.
